key_insight: Thermal expansion from an unsteady Type Ia supernova flame can preheat nearby fuel and sharply shorten carbon ignition times before direct burning occurs.
engineering_relevance: The result identifies mesoscale flame-induced thermodynamic preconditioning as a key mechanism that may affect flame propagation and the onset of deflagration-to-detonation pathways in supernova models.
method: Multidimensional simulations of thermonuclear deflagration fronts
Lagrangian tracer-particle tracking of fuel parcels near the flame
Comparison of low- and high-density models to quantify thermodynamic evolution
evidence_signal: Tracer analysis shows a minority of fuel parcels near the flame undergo modest expansion and heating of about 2×10^8 K to 7×10^8 K, producing substantial ignition-time shortening due to the strong temperature sensitivity of carbon ignition.
watch_item: Nuclear burning was disabled in the analyzed fuel, so the study cannot yet confirm whether this preconditioning actually triggers secondary ignition or detonation.
paper_title: Mesoscale Turbulence in Type Ia Supernova Deflagrations II. Evidence for Fuel Preheat Due to Flame Thermal Expansion from Lagrangian Analysis
